correctness.rationale: From the CAT(0) cone metric, edge ⇔ two circular arc lengths are ≥π. Cliques ⇔ each cyclic gap ≥π. The ordered uniform-simplex density gives exact p and Dirichlet marks. For two k-sets sharing s vertices, all other 2k−s−1 points lie in (k−1) intervals of total length (k−1)δ relative to a common labeled anchor, giving b2=O(n^(−1/(k−1))) at δ=c n^(−k/(k−1)); b1=O(n^−1). General dependency-graph Chen–Stein yields the Poisson TV claim. Markov and a variance bound give both threshold directions. For 3<θ/π<4 the shared-two-vertex double-triangle probability is q=2δ³/(3θ³), yielding the exact variance. All hypotheses and normalized marks stated, and the extracted standard-library checker passed.

originality.rationale: Same-cone prior covers only a 2-point tip passage statistic; the closest public spherical geodesic graph has a distinct bipartite chain structure. General circle U-max and Chen–Stein results supply methods but neither exact k-clique angular characterization and marked law nor the all-order constants and overlap controls. High-level equivalences were compared, with explicit inaccessible-source risks; independent priority confirmation is not claimed.
residual_risks: Unindexed historical Euclidean-cone geodesic clique counts or equivalent circular packing results may exist.

value.rationale: The natural geodesic-passage graph for a singular cone develops all clique orders at distinct sharp angles. The exact conditional Dirichlet marks identify shapes of newly feasible configurations, while the sample-size-dependent Poisson onset and explicit all-order constants quantify when simultaneous tip passage first becomes visible. This is a structural family of geometric and stochastic threshold laws, not a routine finite number or relabeling.
